problem.title: Remove Duplicate Journal Entries by User
problem.prompt: You are working with a mental health app that tracks therapy sessions and journal entries. The `journal_entries` table has accumulated duplicates: some users accidentally submitted the same entry multiple times on the same day. Write a single DELETE statement that removes duplicate journal entries, keeping only the entry with the smallest `entry_id` for each (`user_id`, `entry_date`) pair. After the deletion, write a SELECT statement to confirm the remaining entries, ordered by `user_id`, then `entry_date`, then `entry_id`.
problem.schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE users (user_id INT PRIMARY KEY, username VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL, signup_date DATE NOT NULL); CREATE TABLE journal_entries (entry_id INT PRIMARY KEY, user_id INT NOT NULL, entry_date DATE NOT NULL, mood_rating INT CHECK (mood_rating BETWEEN 1 AND 10), entry_text TEXT, FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users(user_id));
problem.example_input_data: INSERT INTO users (user_id, username, signup_date) VALUES (1, 'alice_m', '2024-01-15'), (2, 'bob_k', '2024-02-01'), (3, 'carol_t', '2024-03-10'); INSERT INTO journal_entries (entry_id, user_id, entry_date, mood_rating, entry_text) VALUES (101, 1, '2024-06-01', 7, 'Feeling better today'), (102, 1, '2024-06-01', 7, 'Feeling better today'), (103, 1, '2024-06-01', 7, 'Feeling better today'), (104, 1, '2024-06-02', 5, 'A bit anxious'), (105, 2, '2024-06-01', 8, 'Great session'), (106, 2, '2024-06-01', 8, 'Great session'), (107, 3, '2024-06-03', 6, 'Reflective mood'), (108, 2, '2024-06-02', 9, 'Very productive day');

composite_moves: keep row with MIN(entry_id) per group
remove all other rows in each group using NOT IN subquery

hints: You need to identify which entry_id values to keep: the smallest one for each combination of user and date.
A subquery with GROUP BY can find the minimum entry_id for each (user_id, entry_date) pair.
Delete rows whose entry_id is NOT IN the set of minimum entry_ids returned by the subquery.
problem.answer_key: DELETE FROM journal_entries WHERE entry_id NOT IN (SELECT MIN(entry_id) FROM journal_entries GROUP BY user_id, entry_date); SELECT * FROM journal_entries ORDER BY user_id, entry_date, entry_id;

_meta.scenario: a mental health app tracking session completion and journal entries
